title: Charcot Triad in Cholangitis: Clinical Context and Pitfalls
subject: Medical Triads
preview: Charcot triad in acute cholangitis comprises fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice.
quickRevision: Charcot triad in acute cholangitis comprises fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice.
Ultrasound and biliary imaging assess obstruction, while antibiotics and timely biliary drainage may be required.
Cholangitis must be differentiated from uncomplicated biliary colic or cholecystitis by systemic illness and cholestatic findings.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Charcot triad in acute cholangitis comprises fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice.
Obstruction and infected bile may progress to bacteremia and sepsis; some patients lack the full classic triad.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Ultrasound and biliary imaging assess obstruction, while antibiotics and timely biliary drainage may be required.
Cholangitis must be differentiated from uncomplicated biliary colic or cholecystitis by systemic illness and cholestatic findings.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: Charcot triad: fever, right-upper-quadrant pain and jaundice.
An incomplete triad does not exclude acute cholangitis.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Absence of the complete triad does not exclude acute cholangitis.
